speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; since the EKG and metabolic panel are normal and your vomiting character and reflux history are pending, I need to clarify if this pain radiates to your jaw or arm and if you have any history of gallstones or recent heavy meals. speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The history of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption followed by choking, coughing, and chest pain is classic for this condition, and the normal cardiac workup further supports this diagnosis. I am requesting images of a Chest X-ray (specifically looking for pneumomediastinum or pleural effusion) to confirm the rupture.
